title: Off-grid 1-tonne solar cold store with grown split array
problem_restatement: Hold 1000 kg fresh produce off-grid on sunlight alone in a stand-on-soil cold box with staged daily intake.
mechanism_sentence: Sunlight makes electricity that charges batteries that run a cooler that blows cold air over produce crates inside a sealed foam box held near 5 °C.
decisive_choices: Chosen grown 3.60 kWp split array 2 on roof plus 7 on ground because 2.40 kWp yielding 9.00 kWh per day is short of 13.2 kWh per day load and 17.6 m2 cannot fit 4.32 m2 roof.

Chosen direct-current variable-speed monoblock with serviceable non-flammable refrigerant because only vapor compression lifts 38 K at 43C ambient while thermal-only or pad-only cannot, with 2.42 percent efficiency cost for village service.
Chosen cam-lock polyisocyanurate box 100 mm walls 120 mm roof and floor because 0.21 W per m2 K gives 203 W conduction within steady budget while thinner foam leaks more.
open_question: Does staged 250 kg per day pull-down hold 5C at 43C ambient on solar-only power as built hardware bench test?
transfer_line: Energy: split photovoltaic array -> battery bank -> monoblock cooler | Measured: return-air probe -> digital thermostat

assumed_constraints.constraint: design for worst-month 5.0 Peak Sun Hours, array equator-facing tilt latitude plus 10 degrees, zero shading 9am-3pm, 0.75 system derate
1 tonne holding at 5C needs 200-350 W steady cooling and 600-900 W peak pull-down; ceiling from door openings and 43C ambient
single mixed holding setpoint 5 degC for 1-tonne mixed produce with 600x400mm vented crates with 25mm air gaps

functional_decomposition: Remove heat from chamber and produce
Enclose chamber against heat and wind
Hold 1 tonne produce in vented crates
Regulate temperature by return-air plus probe control

concept.working_principle: Sun power flows as wire electricity to battery then to cooler then as cold air to crates inside the sealed box with control sensing return air. Fixed-tilt array grown to 3.60 kWp yields 13.5 kWh per day covering 13.2 kWh per day staged load, monoblock holds 5C in PIR box with 203 W conduction plus 0.44 kWh per day door inside 615 W average, staged 250 kg per day in 50 crates.

fabrication_steps.description: Set six precast pads with adjustable feet and raised insulated plinth first, because the box and racking bolt to it and panel loads stay off foam.
Erect cam-lock sandwich box 2.4 by 1.8 by 2.0 m with hinged door plus strip curtain and drain next, because cooler penetration and racks locate inside it.
fabrication_steps.method: Bolt-together PIR panels, 100 mm walls 120 mm roof

fabrication_steps.description: Fit two-row slotted-angle racking and 50 vented 600 by 400 mm crates with 25 mm gaps, because airflow gaps must be set before cooler aiming.
fabrication_steps.method: Bolted galvanized angle, 600 by 400 mm crates

fabrication_steps.description: Mount split array 2 on roof gantry plus 7 on ground frame with screw anchors, set battery box and monoblock with probes, because power-to-cold chain is commissioned last.
fabrication_steps.method: Galvanized tube frames, 400 W modules 1722 by 1134 mm with 48 V battery and monoblock

risks.risk: Small 0.300 kWh per day margin lost on cloudy days
risks.mitigation: Stage 250 kg per day with 8 daytime openings and curtain to stay inside 13.2 kWh per day load.

risks.risk: Wind uplift like 673 kg on 17.6 m2 array
risks.mitigation: Four screw anchors on separate ground frame plus vented roof gantry with no loads into foam.
Single 900 mm door passing one crate at a time with strip curtain and attendant log.

novelty_claim: Grown split shade array with staged crate discipline closing solar-only balance with battery plus eutectic buffer

figure_spec.system_view: Walk-in chamber on six pads with two rack rows and rear high evaporator loop, split array 2 on roof gantry plus 7 on ground frame, battery box at side

open_questions: Does staged 250 kg per day pull-down hold 5C at 43C ambient on solar-only power, requiring built hardware bench test owed to test team?
